## che/homebrew-tap

The homebrew tap serving che: `Formula/che.rb` plus one `Formula/che@<version>.rb` per release, committed by che's release job via the GitLab commits API.

### Why che/homebrew-tap exists?

brew users install and pin che without any GitLab credential; the tap is the anonymous channel.

#### Goals of che/homebrew-tap

- Installation without any GitLab account, in one brew command.
- A specific published version can be pinned.
- The tap is updated by the release itself, so a published release is installable immediately.

### Basic Usage - che/homebrew-tap

#### Installation - che/homebrew-tap

The tap lives on GitLab, so give `brew tap` the repository URL:

```sh
$ brew tap konradodwrot/che https://gitlab.com/konradodwrot/che/homebrew-tap.git
$ brew install che
```

Pin a version through its versioned formula:

```sh
$ brew install che@0.0.152
```

#### Usage - che/homebrew-tap

Once tapped, `che` upgrades with the rest of your formulae:

```sh
$ brew upgrade che
```

`Formula/che.rb` tracks the latest release; each `Formula/che@<version>.rb` stays pinned to the version it names, so an older one remains installable after newer releases land.

Nothing here is edited by hand: che's release job commits every formula through the GitLab commits API.
